mainTopic: How a ship is acquired (משיכה or מסירה, depending on location and the seller's words), and the wording needed to sell a שטר.
overview: The גמרא finishes pointing out a contradiction between two ברייתות about buying a ship. In one, רבי seems to hold that a ship is acquired by pulling (משיכה). In the other, he says handing over (מסירה) is enough. The גמרא first answers that the ברייתות speak of different places: the public domain and an alleyway. It then attacks that answer. No one owns the public domain to rent it out, and אביי and רבא rule that משיכה does not work there. So the גמרא re-reads the חכמים: pull the ship into an alleyway, or rent its spot if it sits in someone's private area. When this makes אביי and רבא seem to follow only רבי, רב אשי explains that everyone accepts מסירה. The dispute is only about a seller who said 'go pull and acquire': was he insisting, or just suggesting? Then a new topic begins. רב פפא rules that someone selling a שטר must write 'acquire it and all the liens in it.' Otherwise the buyer may get only the paper, even if all he could do with it is plug a bottle.

steps.title: Finishing the quote that creates the contradiction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא in which the חכמים say a ship is not acquired until it is pulled or its place is rented. This closes the challenge against the earlier ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: …until he pulls it, or until he rents its place!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of a second ברייתא that clashes with the first one. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this second ברייתא, רבי holds that a ship is acquired through מסירה, and the חכמים require משיכה or renting the place. That clashes with the earlier ברייתא, which seemed to have רבי holding that a ship is acquired through משיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulling: acquiring an item by drawing it toward yourself
Handing over: acquiring by taking hold of the item's rope or reins from the seller
Renting the place where the item sits

phrases.english: until he pulls it
or until he rents its place!

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁיִּמְשְׁכֶנָּה אוֹ עַד שֶׁיִּשְׂכּוֹר אֶת מְקוֹמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contradiction raised just before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier ברייתא, which had רבי holding that a ship is acquired through משיכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In this ברייתא רבי says מסירה, while the earlier one had him saying משיכה.

steps.title: Different locations: public domain versus alleyway
steps.stepSummary: The two ברייתות do not argue. One speaks of a ship in the public domain, where מסירה works. The other speaks of a ship in an alleyway, where משיכה works.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, it is in the public domain; there, it is in an alleyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying each ברייתא is talking about a ship in a different place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא with רבי saying מסירה speaks of the public domain. The one requiring משיכה speaks of a סמטא, a side alley. Each method of acquisition works in its own type of place.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources speak about different cases
Public domain
An alleyway or side area, between public and private

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
here, in the public domain,
phrases.notes: This "here" is the ברייתא where רבי says handing over works.

phrases.english: there, in an alleyway.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא; כָּאן בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, כָּאן בְּסִימְטָא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to give רבי two different methods for the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second ברייתא is about the public domain (מסירה); the first is about an alleyway (משיכה).

steps.title: Who can you rent from in the public domain?
steps.stepSummary: If the second ברייתא is about the public domain, the חכמים's option of renting the ship's place makes no sense. Nobody owns the public domain, so there is no one to rent from.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain the latter ברייתא? As being about the public domain? Then look at its last clause: the חכמים say he does not acquire until he pulls it. But if it is in the public domain, from whom would he rent?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It uses the חכמים's words in the same ברייתא to show that a public-domain setting does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Renting a place assumes the place has an owner. Public property has no owner to rent from, so the חכמים's "or until he rents its place" cannot be about the public domain.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case did you set it?
Look at the last clause
From whom does he rent?

phrases.english: In what case did you set
this latter one? In the public domain?
Then say the latter clause:

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: לֹא קָנָה עַד שֶׁיִּמְשְׁכֶנָּה.
phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: he does not acquire until he pulls it.
phrases.notes: The quote is cut short. It goes on "or until he rents its place," which is the part being questioned here.

phrases.english: But if it is in the public domain,
from whom does he rent?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the location-based answer of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the second ברייתא is about the public domain.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים mention renting the place, but no one owns the public domain to rent it out.

steps.title: Pulling does not work in the public domain
steps.stepSummary: There is a second problem. According to אביי and רבא, משיכה does not acquire in the public domain at all. So how could the חכמים require pulling there?
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, does pulling acquire in the public domain? Don't אביי and רבא both say: handing over acquires in the public domain and in a courtyard that belongs to neither of them; pulling acquires in an alleyway and in a courtyard belonging to both of them; and lifting acquires everywhere!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second attack on the same answer. It brings a rule from אביי and רבא that limits where each method of acquisition works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי and רבא assign each method to its places: מסירה in the public domain, משיכה in an alley or a jointly owned courtyard, and הגבהה anywhere. If the case is in the public domain, the חכמים's demand for משיכה seems to contradict this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; introduces an additional challenge
Lifting: acquiring by raising the item up
A courtyard owned jointly by buyer and seller
Both of them

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of אביי and רבא is a basic map of where each קנין works. It is used across many סוגיות about acquiring movable property.

phrases.aramaic: וְתוּ, מְשִׁיכָה בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים מִי קָנְיָא?!
phrases.english: And furthermore, does pulling acquire in the public domain?!
But don't Abaye and Rava both say:
Handing over acquires in the public domain,
and in a courtyard that does not belong to either of them;
pulling acquires in an alleyway,
and in a courtyard that belongs to both of them;
and lifting acquires in every place!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, מְשִׁיכָה בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים מִי קָנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to the same answer from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the חכמים in the second ברייתא speak about the public domain.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי and רבא rule that משיכה does not acquire in the public domain, yet the חכמים require משיכה there.

steps.title: Re-reading the חכמים: pull it into an alley, or rent a private spot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains what the חכמים really mean. "Until he pulls it" means pulling the ship out of the public domain into an alleyway. "Renting its place" applies only when the ship sits in someone's private domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does it mean when it says "until he pulls it," and what does it mean when it says "until he rents its place"? This is what it is saying: until he pulls it from the public domain into an alleyway. And if it is in an owner's domain, he does not acquire it until he rents its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers both challenges by giving a new reading of the חכמים's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pulling counts once the ship ends up in a סמטא, where משיכה works, so the rule of אביי and רבא is kept. Renting is a separate case: a ship in a privately owned area, where there is an owner to rent from. The public-domain setting can therefore stand.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means; introduces a re-reading of a source
A domain that belongs to an owner

steps.whatToRemember: A ship in the public domain: רבי says מסירה is enough. The חכמים say it must be pulled into an alleyway, or, if it sits in someone's private area, its place must be rented.
steps.confusionAlert: "Or until he rents its place" is not a second option for the same public-domain ship. It is a different case: a ship sitting in privately owned space.

phrases.english: What does it mean when it says "until he pulls it";
and what does it mean when it says "until he rents its place"?
This is what it is saying:
until he pulls it from the public domain into an alleyway;
and if it is an owner's domain,

phrases.aramaic: לָא קָנָה עַד שֶׁיִּשְׂכּוֹר אֶת מְקוֹמָהּ.
phrases.english: he does not acquire until he rents its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both challenges from steps 3 and 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים seemed to require pulling or renting while the ship stays in the public domain.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pulling means bringing the ship into an alleyway. Renting applies only when the ship is in a privately owned domain.

steps.title: Do אביי and רבא hold only like רבי?
steps.stepSummary: Since the חכמים require pulling the ship into an alleyway, it seems only רבי accepts מסירה in the public domain. That would make אביי and רבא follow the minority view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that אביי and רבא hold like רבי (and not like the חכמים)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the rule of אביי and רבא, that מסירה works in the public domain, matches only רבי's view in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 explained that the חכמים want the ship pulled out of the public domain into an alleyway. That sounds like the חכמים reject מסירה in the public domain. If so, אביי and רבא, who accept it there, would be siding with רבי against the majority. That is an uncomfortable position.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא usually goes on to reject)
Acquiring by taking hold of the animal's reins or the ship's ropes

phrases.english: Shall we say that אביי and רבא
state their view in accordance with רבי?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer in step 5, which made the חכמים seem to reject מסירה in the public domain
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of אביי and רבא that מסירה acquires in the public domain
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the חכמים require pulling into an alleyway, only רבי accepts מסירה in the public domain. That leaves אביי and רבא following a minority opinion.

steps.title: It depends on what the seller told the buyer
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי: if the seller said 'go take possession and acquire,' the חכמים agree that מסירה works. The ברייתא is about a seller who said 'go pull and acquire.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: If the seller told him, 'Go take possession and acquire,' then indeed everyone agrees he acquires through מסירה. Here we are dealing with a seller who told him, 'Go pull and acquire.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends אביי and רבא. He shows that the חכמים do accept מסירה in the public domain, and that the ברייתא is about a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument in the ברייתא is not about whether מסירה works. It is about a seller who mentioned pulling by name. When the seller gives open permission ('take possession'), even the חכמים accept מסירה, so אביי and רבא fit everyone's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Go take possession and acquire (general permission to use any method)
Go pull and acquire (the seller names a specific method)
So too / indeed, that is so

steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that the חכמים reject מסירה in the public domain. Their disagreement with רבי is only about a seller who said 'go pull.'

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
If the seller said to him, 'Go take possession and acquire,'
so it is indeed (he acquires through מסירה);
phrases.notes: He means that even the חכמים agree in this case.

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
where he said to him, 'Go pull and acquire.'

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא's dispute concerns a seller who told the buyer to pull
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים reject מסירה in the public domain entirely
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone accepts מסירה when the seller gave general permission. The dispute arises only when the seller said 'go pull.'

steps.title: The real dispute: was the seller insisting?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים hold that the seller insists on pulling. רבי holds that the seller was only suggesting a method.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master (the חכמים) holds the seller is particular about the method. The other master (רבי) holds the seller is just showing him a way to acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finishes his answer by explaining what רבי and the חכמים actually argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a seller says 'go pull and acquire,' the חכמים read it as a condition: only pulling counts. רבי reads it as friendly advice, so any valid method, including מסירה, still works. The question is about the seller's intent, not about what kinds of acquisition work.

keyTerms.meaning: Being particular / insisting on a specific way
Just pointing out a way (a suggestion, not a demand)
One master holds

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees מסירה works in the public domain. רבי and the חכמים argue only about whether 'go pull and acquire' is a strict demand or a mere suggestion. So אביי and רבא fit all opinions.

phrases.english: One master holds: he is particular,
phrases.notes: This is the חכמים: the seller wants only pulling, so מסירה won't work here.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: מַרְאֶה מָקוֹם הוּא לוֹ.
phrases.english: and one master holds: he is just showing him a way.
phrases.notes: This is רבי: the seller doesn't mind which valid method the buyer uses.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר קְפִידָא וּמָר סָבַר מַרְאֶה מָקוֹם הוּא לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the case narrowed in step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the dispute as a question of the seller's intent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute is about whether מסירה works in the public domain
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is about whether 'go pull' is a strict demand or a suggestion

steps.title: Selling a שטר needs special wording
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא: someone who sells a שטר to another must write, 'Acquire it and all the liens in it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Someone who sells a שטר to his friend must write for him: 'Acquire it and all the liens that are in it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: how a loan document is transferred when it is sold. רב פפא gives a rule about the wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שטר is both a piece of paper and a right to collect money, backed by liens on the borrower's property. רב פפא says the seller must spell out that the buyer gets the paper together with all the collection rights behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: A document, here a loan document
A lien, the right to collect from the borrower's property
Sells

phrases.english: רב פפא said:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי מַאן דִּמְזַבֵּין לֵיהּ שְׁטָרָא לְחַבְרֵיהּ,
phrases.english: One who sells a document to his friend
must write for him:
'Acquire it, and all the liens that are in it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא הַאי מַאן דִּמְזַבֵּין לֵיהּ שְׁטָרָא לְחַבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic, selling loan documents
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When selling a שטר, the seller must write 'acquire it and all the liens in it.'

steps.title: Without that wording, does the buyer not acquire?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that he asked רב כהנא about רב פפא's rule: does it mean that without this wording, the buyer does not acquire?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I said this teaching before רב כהנא, and I said to him: The reason the buyer acquires is that the seller wrote this. So if he did not write this, he does not acquire?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי tests רב פפא's rule by drawing out what it implies. The גמרא is setting up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the special wording is what makes the sale work, then a sale without it should fail. רב אשי raises this conclusion as a question to examine whether it is really correct.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching / a ruling
Before him / in his presence
The reason is because (this introduces a precise reading of a ruling)

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
I said this teaching before רב כהנא,
and I said to him:
The reason he acquires is that he wrote this for him,

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָא כְּתַב לֵיהּ הָכִי – לָא קָנֵי?
phrases.english: so if he did not write this for him, he does not acquire?

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דִּכְתַב לֵיהּ הָכִי הָא לָא כְּתַב לֵיהּ הָכִי לָא קָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines what follows from רב פפא's ruling in step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, by רב פפא's rule, a buyer of a שטר fails to acquire if the seller left out the phrase about the liens

steps.title: Would anyone buy a document just to plug a bottle?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי argues that the buyer of a שטר obviously wants the debt, not the paper. So the buyer should get the debt even without the special wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does he need it just to tie over the mouth of his flask?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי continues his question from the last step. He points out how strange it would be if the buyer only got the paper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the buyer acquires only the paper, he has bought something almost worthless, good only as a bottle stopper. Nobody pays for a שטר for that reason. So רב אשי suggests the sale should automatically include the debt, and the special wording in רב פפא's rule should not be needed.

keyTerms.meaning: to tie, to wrap around or seal
a small flask or bottle
over the mouth (opening) of
'But is it really...?', a word that opens a pointed, challenging question

phrases.english: But to tie over the mouth of his flask
does he need it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי לָצוֹר עַל פִּי צְלוֹחִיתוֹ הוּא צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the reasoning behind the question in step 10. It turns that question into a direct challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's rule that the seller must write 'Acquire it and all the liens in it'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A buyer clearly pays for a שטר to collect the debt, not for the paper. So the debt should transfer automatically, and the wording should not be needed.

steps.title: Yes, he may have bought it only for the paper
steps.stepSummary: The answer: yes, without the proper wording we say the buyer may have wanted only the paper, even just to plug a bottle.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: Yes. To tie, and to tie.
steps.whatsHappening: The one רב אשי asked answers his challenge and stands by רב פפא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer accepts what רב אשי called strange: it is possible to buy a שטר only for the paper. Since the seller never clearly passed on the rights to the debt, the buyer gets only what he physically received, which is the paper. That is why the words 'acquire it and all the liens in it' are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: yes (Aramaic)
'to tie, and to tie': yes, really just for tying

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב פפא, selling a שטר without saying 'acquire it and all the liens in it' passes on only the paper, not the right to collect the debt.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the answer is saying that buyers usually want bottle stoppers. It only means that without clear wording, the sale cannot be assumed to include the debt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the debt in a שטר is something separate from the paper. The seller has to pass it on in clear words.

phrases.english: He said to me: Yes;
to tie, and to tie.
phrases.notes: Saying it twice is like saying 'yes, really, just for tying.' Without the wording, he may have bought only the paper.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 11 by accepting its strange-sounding conclusion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the challenger's conclusion: yes, the buyer may have bought just the paper
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A buyer surely wants the debt, so the debt should transfer even without the special wording.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without 'acquire it and all the liens in it,' the buyer gets only the paper. That paper could be used for something as minor as sealing a bottle.
